title: Hubble sees galaxies galore
caption: The Hubble Ultra Deep Field, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: Hubble Ultra Deep Field, HUDF · constellation Fornax
credit: NASA, ESA, and S. Beckwith (STScI) and the HUDF Team

recognition.text: Ranked #12 on ESA/Hubble’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: Almost every speck in this picture is a galaxy, nearly 10,000 of them in many ages, sizes, shapes and colors. This is the Hubble Ultra Deep Field, described as the deepest visible-light image of the cosmos, a narrow core sample of the universe reaching across billions of light-years.

The nearest galaxies are the larger, well-defined spirals and ellipticals, seen as they were about 1 billion years ago. The smallest and reddest, around 100 of them, may be among the most distant known, glimpsed when the universe was only 800 million years old. In between is a zoo of oddballs. Some resemble toothpicks, others look like links in a bracelet, and a few appear to be interacting. They record a younger, more chaotic era when order was only starting to appear.

The patch of sky is tiny, just one-tenth the width of the full Moon, in the constellation Fornax, and from the ground it looks almost empty. Hubble needed 800 exposures over 400 orbits of Earth to build it.

understand.summary: Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys recorded this field in visible and near-infrared light. Blue and green show light the eye can see, such as from hot young stars and Sun-like stars, while red represents near-infrared light, such as the glow of dust-enshrouded galaxies.
understand.eye: The near-infrared light shown as red is invisible to the human eye, and ground-based photographs show this patch of sky as largely empty.

explore: The total exposure time added up to 11.3 days. Looking into the field has been compared to peering through a soda straw 2.5 meters long, and the region is so empty of nearby stars that only a handful from our own Milky Way appear in the frame.
alt: A black field crowded with thousands of galaxies of different sizes, shapes and colors, from large spirals and ellipticals to tiny red specks.
